scope_stop_message: This checker covers drinks up to 1.2% ABV. Higher-ABV drinks fall under different rules that aren't covered here.
scope_description: Checks UK import basics for soft drinks at or below 1.2% ABV: the Soft Drinks Industry Levy, UK Food Business Operator address, EORI registration, mandatory label information, proof of origin, and commercial invoice readiness.
disclaimer: This is general guidance based on the cited government sources, not legal advice. Confirm your specific situation with HMRC or a customs specialist before relying on it.

sources: Soft Drinks Industry Levy — scope and rates
Soft Drinks Industry Levy — small producer exemption
rules.primary_source: Soft Drinks Industry Levy — scope and rates

text.not_applicable: Added sugar is below {lower_band_min_g_per_100ml}g per 100ml, so the Soft Drinks Industry Levy does not apply to this product.
text.action_needed: This product falls in the {band} Soft Drinks Industry Levy band (added sugar of {sugar}g per 100ml). Since you import {annual_volume_desc} annually, SDIL registration is likely required.
text.confirm: This product falls in the {band} Soft Drinks Industry Levy band (added sugar of {sugar}g per 100ml). The small-producer exemption is based on production volume, and whether it applies to an importer bringing in someone else's product needs confirming with HMRC.

sources: UK Food Business Operator (FBO) address requirement
rules.primary_source: UK Food Business Operator (FBO) address requirement

text.action_needed_no_importer: Appoint a UK-based importer or distributor to act as the Food Business Operator, or establish a UK entity, before placing this product on the UK market.
text.action_needed_no_address: The label does not show a UK Food Business Operator address. Add the UK importer's or distributor's name and address to the label.
text.confirm_address_unknown: Confirm whether the label shows a UK Food Business Operator name and address, as required once you have a UK importer.
text.covered: The label shows a UK Food Business Operator address, as required.

sources: EORI number required to import into the UK
rules.primary_source: EORI number required to import into the UK

text.action_needed: Apply for an EORI number before importing into the UK; it's required for customs clearance.
text.confirm: Confirm that your importer has a valid EORI number before the shipment reaches UK customs.
text.covered: Your importer has an EORI number, as required for customs clearance.

sources: Mandatory label information under UK FIC (Food Information for Consumers)
rules.primary_source: Mandatory label information under UK FIC (Food Information for Consumers)

element_labels.ingredients_list_with_allergens: an ingredients list with allergens highlighted

text.action_needed: Add the following required label information: {missing}.
text.confirm: Confirm whether an origin statement is required for this product; the source lists it as required "where applicable".
text.covered: The label includes the English name, an ingredients list with allergens highlighted, and an origin statement.

sources: Rules of Origin for tariff-free UK-EU trade
rules.primary_source: Rules of Origin for tariff-free UK-EU trade

text.action_needed: Obtain proof of origin for this product to qualify for tariff-free treatment under the UK-EU trade agreement.
text.confirm: Confirm that proof of origin will be available for this shipment to qualify for tariff-free treatment.
text.covered: Proof of origin is available for this product.

sources: Commercial invoice requirements for UK customs clearance
rules.primary_source: Commercial invoice requirements for UK customs clearance

text.action_needed: Prepare a commercial invoice that includes: EORI numbers for both sender and buyer, tariff/commodity codes, country of origin, Incoterms, and any relevant certifications.
text.confirm: Confirm the commercial invoice will include: EORI numbers for both sender and buyer, tariff/commodity codes, country of origin, Incoterms, and any relevant certifications.
text.covered: The commercial invoice includes EORI numbers for both sender and buyer, tariff/commodity codes, country of origin, Incoterms, and relevant certifications.
